title: Stoner transitions beyond mean-field in two-dimensional electronic systems: a diagrammatic Monte Carlo study
authors: Yueh-Chen Lee, Nikolay P. Prokof'ev, Andrey V. Chubukov
abstract: Stoner instabilities for fermions with repulsive interaction have been well studied within the mean-field (ladder) approximation. In this study, we consider two-dimensional electronic systems with one or two valleys and discuss a Stoner transition beyond the ladder approximation. At weak coupling, the corrections to the ladder approximation come predominantly from the renormalization of the particle-hole vertex in the particle-particle channel, and the lowest-order corrections are logarithmically singular in the low-density limit. To investigate the problem beyond the lowest order, we apply the diagrammatic Monte Carlo algorithm and treat ladder and non-ladder renormalizations on equal footing. We find that in a one-valley system, a Stoner transition to a ferromagnetism occurs at low density only if there is a cutoff on the momentum transfer carried by the interaction. In a two-valley system, the restriction is less severe. Here we find either a direct Stoner transition into a spin- and valley-polarized state, or a set of two Stoner transitions via an intermediate valley-polarized state. The pathway is controlled by the anisotropy of the fermionic dispersion.
summary: This paper rigorously examines Stoner transitions in 2D electronic materials by moving beyond mean-field approximations using a Diagrammatic Monte Carlo simulation. The study reveals that the nature of magnetic ordering—whether it occurs, and through what sequence of phases—is highly dependent on the number of valleys and the anisotropy of the underlying electron dispersion. It provides crucial insights into correlated magnetism in low-dimensional quantum materials.
main_problem: The study investigates Stoner instabilities in two-dimensional electronic systems, going beyond the limitations of mean-field theory.
main_result: In one-valley systems, ferromagnetism only occurs if momentum transfer is cut off; for two-valley systems, the transition can be direct or proceed through an intermediate valley-polarized state, controlled by dispersion anisotropy.
method: The authors employ a diagrammatic Monte Carlo (DiagMC) algorithm to treat both ladder and non-ladder renormalizations on equal footing in the susceptibility calculation.
model_or_system: The system models 2D electronic systems with one or two valleys, described by Hamiltonians including kinetic terms and repulsive interactions. The analysis considers parabolic ($k^2$) and $k^6$ dispersions for single-valley cases, and elliptic dispersion for two-valley setups.
key_observables: Stoner transition point (instability), order parameters like valley polarization (VP) and ferromagnetism (FM), and the static magnetic susceptibility ($\chi_s$).
important_parameters: Dimensionless coupling constant $\lambda$, momentum cutoff $q^*$, and anisotropy factor $\eta$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is extending beyond mean-field theory by including higher-order diagrammatic corrections via the DiagMC method.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams for single-valley and two-valley systems showing symmetry-breaking phases (e.g., VP, SVP) versus interaction parameters ($q^*$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the mean-field context to applying the advanced DiagMC technique to calculate susceptibilities beyond lowest order, culminating in detailed phase diagrams mapping out different magnetic/valley ordered states.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of diagrammatic Monte Carlo techniques for strongly correlated electron systems provides sophisticated computational tools applicable to other many-body quantum problems where perturbative expansions fail.
